column1: # Donkey Kong Bananza (Switch 2, update v458752). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive), SDK 20.5.19, NVN2 (the Switch 2's NVN: Ampere shaders, DLSS); modules main + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/, updates/<version>/, dlc/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (not measured here): with the guessed Switch 1 pool (3.2 GB) the game's heaps did not fit (AudioSystemHeap creation returned null, main+0x564b48).
# 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 9 GB heap region
# The NPDM declares no system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, and the game sets a heap (without the key the host answers 32 MB, and the SDK's VammManager
# asks GetInfo 0x21, which Switch 1 kernels do not have, for the size to map up front)
# Draw passes ordered by the game's own barriers (nvn_mtl.m barrier_game): with the default full barrier every one of the ~120 draw passes a frame waited for all earlier GPU work,
# so the ~70 small post-processing passes at the frame's end ran one after another. 2026-11-23, M1 Max, checkpoint route at ~26,200 draws: frame 21.28 -> 20.26 ms (47 -> 49 fps),
# GPU tail after translation 5.2 -> 4.2 ms; screen-recording flicker check and 90 s screenshot unchanged. DM_NVN_BARRIER=full restores the full barriers
# At most 1 split of one long render pass while the GPU waits (nvn_mtl.m pass_split_try; the default is 2): each split stores and loads the G-buffer. M1 Max, checkpoint route
# (~26,200 draws, 2 runs each). 2026-11-23, with ~16 ms of translation: limit 6 18.56 ms a frame, 4 18.30-18.41 (p95 20.9 -> 19.8, GPU 12.05 -> 11.46 ms), none 19.41.
# 2026-11-24, with ~9.5 ms of translation: limit 4 GPU p50 11.36 ms / frame p99 18.49, 2 11.45 / 17.54, 1 11.05 / 18.11, none 11.01 / 20.54: one split starts the GPU early enough.
